newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel oil barges keep firming on low supply.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel oil barges keep firming on low supply.

text.p: European high sulphur barges firmed to two-month highs on Friday with barge players said to be short cover buying after large cargo volumes leaked out of the region, traders said.
After Thursday's strong showing business began at $86.75 a tonne before gaining in quarter dollar increments to touch $88, a level not seen since mid-March.
Opinions differed on the sustainability of the upturn given fuel oil is traditionally weak in the summer, and on how much of the rise was manipulative or really the result of supply shortages.
"We'll definitely be firm for the next few days, as we know we are short material up to the 15th," said one trader.
Antwerp reported good bunker demand while Rotterdam was thin and some players felt the bubble would burst next week if bunker interest slumps.
"There is a bit of a game going on and I'm not convinced all this strength is from short covering," said an Antwerp trader.
Large volumes of fuel oil were reported to have left NWE for the U.S. Atlantic coast recently, or to fill the holes left in Med supply by arbing out to the Far East.

There was little sign of Russian cracked material, with one cargo in the hands of a trader being chased by multiple buyers. Cif and fob cargo numbers moved apart because of higher freight rates, traders said.
"Ships seem to be tied up for longer," said one buyer. "They are not necessarily moving more material but they appear to be having to move it further.
